refuter_votes.reason: Paragraph 5.4 is an operative procurement rule, not merely an enabling clause: within its stated value band, entities must invite only Australian businesses. Its exceptions qualify the rule but do not erase the exclusion it imposes when applicable.

P2-I1 expressly covers exclusions for a threshold band. The Australian-business-only invitation rule is evidence of an operative exclusion, so it supports a score of 1 under the rubric; the standing-offer carveout and documented inapplicability exception do not negate that measure.

The quoted text says the entities “must invite only Australian businesses” for the specified procurements, directly establishing restricted invitation eligibility. It does not establish a foreign-ownership ban, but P2-I1 does not require one; the rule concerns who may be invited to public procurement.
